transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump marked Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports he also defended the war with Iran as necessary.
President Trump recounted stories of heroism and grave injury of troops
who served in past American wars before turning to the ongoing conflict with Iran.
As he has many times, Trump argued that Iran had been at war with America since 1979,
and it was about time the U.S. responded.
And we seriously fought back, and we won.
It's just a question of wouldn't we want to end it?
We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93 percent victory.
It's going to be total.
This isn't the first time Trump has claimed the war has been won.
His plan for getting to 100 percent victory remains unclear.
Tamara Keith, NPR News, the White House.
Democrats preparing to take control of Congress in January
are pressing ahead with plans to investigate the Trump administration.
The White House has warned those inquiries could cross the line into what it calls federal criminality.
California Congressman Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee,
tells MS Now that warning won't deter the incoming majority.
The reality is that we're not going to be intimidated by the president.
We're not going to be intimidated by anyone in our work.
Our work is about taking on government corruption,
making life more affordable through bringing down costs
by actually going after the crooks and the criminals that are causing harm.
The White House issued the warning in a letter accusing Garcia
of trying to intimidate administration officials.
Garcia says Congress has the authority to conduct oversight without permission from the White House.
Russia's ambassador to the United States has died.
The news was confirmed by Russia's foreign ministry
and comes as the Trump administration is seeking to engage Russia diplomatically over Ukraine and other issues.
From Moscow, NPR's Charles Maines reports.
Alexander Darcheev was a student of the Americas,
serving as Russia's ambassador to Canada and other related posts
before assuming the role of ambassador to the U.S. last year.
In a post online, the foreign ministry spokesperson said Darcheev died in Moscow due to chronic disease.
A formal ministry statement announcing his passing also praised Darcheev
as an outstanding diplomat, colleague and mentor.
In his short tenure in Washington, Darcheev often echoed Kremlin warnings
against the U.S.'s military support for Ukraine
and led Russia in negotiations with the Trump administration aimed at improving ties.
He also made fewer headlines than his immediate predecessors
who had to answer for allegations of Kremlin interference in U.S. elections during Trump's first term.
Darcheev was 66 years old.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Pope Leo leaves Argentina today for the final leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America
in his last days in the South American country.
He spoke to prisoners, survivors of Argentina's dirty war,
and to young people warning of the ills of vanity.
NPR's Carrie Cahn reports.
Crowds have been massive for the Pope's packed schedule.
In Argentina, he told a huge gathering of young Argentines and Buenos Aires
to reject "idols of our time."
He warned against a long list of dangers, including money, drugs, porn,
and an obsession with popularity, appearance, and pleasure.
Leo urged youth to "not bow down before anything that cannot give you life."
Anticipation for Leo's Peru visit is huge.
The pontiff lived here for two decades and became a naturalized Peruvian citizen.
The Vatican is calling his Peru Stapa homecoming.
Peruvian officials launched a Pope weather watch
as much of the country is under a state of emergency with heavy rains forecast due to El Nino.
Carrie Cahn, NPR News, Chicleo, Peru.
Workers across Spain walked off the job today demanding action on soaring housing costs.
The country's two largest unions backed the general strike
disrupting transportation and closing businesses.
Demonstrators want stronger protections for tenants,
more public housing, and limits on property speculation.
In Madrid, police used pepper spray
and pushed protesters off a major shopping street.
The protests come ahead of Spain's national election later this month.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump marks Veterans Day at Arlington, defends Iran war as necessary to achieve total victory
Democrats in Congress vow to pursue Trump administration investigations despite White House warnings
Russian ambassador to the U.S. Alexander Darchiev dies at age 66 in Moscow
Pope Leo tells Argentine youth to reject idols like money, drugs, and vanity
Pope Leo arrives in Peru for homecoming visit amid El Nino emergency and heavy rain
Workers across Spain strike over soaring housing costs, with police pepper-spraying Madrid protesters
